title: Stochastic Matrix Has An Invariant Distribution
body_html:
Stochastic Matrix Has An Invariant Distribution

Every finite stochastic matrix has an invariant distribution.
proof_html:
Let $A$ be a square stochastic matrix and put $B=A-\operatorname{Id}$. In the zero-sum game with payoff matrix $B$, the uniform mixed strategy of player 2 guarantees payoff at most $0$ for player 1, so the value is at most $0$.

Conversely, against any mixed column $y$, player 1 can choose a row $i$ with $y_i=\min_j y_j$. Since the row of $A$ is a probability vector, $$ (Ay)_i-y_i=\sum_j A_{ij}y_j-y_i\ge 0. $$ Therefore player 1 can guarantee at least $0$, and the value of $B$ is $0$. If $x^*$ is an optimal strategy of player 1, then $$ x^*A-x^*\ge 0. $$ Pairing with the uniform vector gives equality of the total mass, hence every component is actually zero and $x^*A=x^*$. Thus $x^*$ is an invariant distribution.

References

  • [MFoGT, Cor. 2.5.2] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Invariant distribution of a stochastic matrix from minimax.
